stories.actor: Ze'eiri and Rabbi Yochanan
stories.event: Ze'eiri avoided marrying Rabbi Yochanan's daughter, but carried him across a puddle on his shoulders.
stories.turn: Rabbi Yochanan used the act of respect to challenge him: our Torah is fit for you but our daughters are not?
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yochanan argued that Babylonian lineage is no purer, though the Gemara notes he had missed Rabbi Elazar's teaching that Ezra purified Babylonia.
stories.summary: Ze'eiri kept avoiding Rabbi Yochanan, who wanted him to marry his daughter. When they came to a puddle, Ze'eiri carried Rabbi Yochanan across on his shoulders. Rabbi Yochanan asked why the Torah of Eretz Yisrael was worthy of his honor but its daughters were not, and argued that flawed families also remained in Babylonia.

stories.actor: Ulla and Rav Yehuda
stories.event: Visiting Rav Yehuda in Pumbedita, Ulla saw his grown son unmarried and asked why.
stories.turn: Rav Yehuda said he could not find a family of sure lineage, and Ulla answered that nobody knows where they come from.
stories.outcome: When Rav Yehuda asked what to do, Ulla told him to look for families whose members fall silent first in a quarrel.
stories.summary: Ulla came to Rav Yehuda's house and saw that his son Rav Yitzchak was grown but unmarried. Rav Yehuda explained he was worried about lineage. Ulla replied that no one can be sure of his own ancestry, citing verses about ravished women and immoral people. When Rav Yehuda asked what to do, Ulla advised him to follow the practice in Eretz Yisrael and choose the family that is first to fall silent in a quarrel.

stories.actor: A man and Rav Pappa
stories.event: A man sold land to Rav Pappa because he needed money to buy oxen.
stories.turn: In the end he did not need the money.
stories.outcome: Rav Pappa returned the land to him, beyond the letter of the law.
stories.summary: A man sold land to Rav Pappa to raise money for oxen. When it turned out he did not need the money, Rav Pappa gave the land back, which the Gemara says was beyond what the law required.

stories.actor: The residents of Neharde'a and Rav Nachman
stories.event: During a drought in Neharde'a everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat.
stories.turn: Wheat then arrived, and it turned out the ship had already been nearby when they sold.
stories.outcome: Rav Nachman ruled the mansions returned to their owners, and defended the ruling against Rami bar Shmuel's objection.
stories.summary: A drought struck Neharde'a and everyone sold their mansions to buy wheat. Then wheat arrived, the ship having already been close by at the time of the sales. Rav Nachman ruled that the mansions go back to their owners. Rami bar Shmuel objected that this would discourage future buyers; Rav Nachman asked whether droughts happen every day, and Rami replied that in Neharde'a they do.

stories.actor: The Sages, Rav, Shmuel and Karna
stories.event: After Shmuel ruled that a minor betrothed without her father's consent needs both a bill of divorce and refusal, and Karna mocked the ruling, the Sages sent the question to Rav with the names swapped.
stories.turn: Rav, thinking Shmuel held the opposite view, swore by God that both are required.
stories.outcome: Rav ended up endorsing Shmuel's ruling, saying it was unthinkable for Shmuel to say otherwise.
stories.summary: Shmuel ruled that a minor betrothed without her father's consent needs both a bill of divorce and refusal, and Karna called this self-contradictory. The Sages sent the question to Rav, reversing who said what. Rav swore that she needs both, and said God forbid that Shmuel should say otherwise.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yochanan's relatives
stories.event: Rabbi Yochanan's relatives seized orphans' cow in an alley for a debt.
stories.turn: Rabbi Yochanan approved the seizure, but Reish Lakish told them to return it.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yochanan told them he could do nothing, since a colleague of equal stature disagreed with him.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yochanan's relatives took a cow belonging to orphans to pay a debt their father owed. Rabbi Yochanan said the seizure was valid, but Reish Lakish ordered them to give it back. When they complained to Rabbi Yochanan, he said there was nothing he could do because someone of his stature disagreed.

stories.actor: A herdsman of orphans and a creditor
stories.event: A creditor seized an ox from the orphans' herdsman; they disputed whether this was before or after the debtor's death.
stories.turn: Rav Nachman asked the herdsman for witnesses, and he had none.
stories.outcome: Rav Nachman ruled for the creditor, who could have claimed he bought the ox.
stories.summary: A creditor took an ox from the herdsman of some orphans, claiming he seized it while their father was alive; the herdsman said it was after his death. Before Rav Nachman, the herdsman admitted he had no witnesses to the seizure. Rav Nachman ruled that since the creditor could have claimed he bought the ox, his claim stands.

stories.actor: The house of the Nasi and Rabbi Abba
stories.event: The Nasi's household seized an orphans' maidservant in an alley for a debt.
stories.turn: Rabbi Abbahu approved the seizure, but Rabbi Abba accused the judges of currying favor with the powerful.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Abba cited Reish Lakish's reversal of a ruling following Rabbi Tarfon.
stories.summary: Members of the Nasi's household seized a maidservant belonging to orphans for a debt. Rabbi Abbahu, sitting in judgment with colleagues, said the seizure was fine. Rabbi Abba, sitting with them, asked whether they were flattering the Nasi's house, pointing out that Reish Lakish had overturned such a ruling before.

stories.actor: Yeimar bar Chashu, Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
stories.event: Yeimar bar Chashu sent an agent to seize a dead debtor's boat.
stories.turn: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna told the agent his seizure was invalid because it harmed other creditors, then seized the boat themselves, each claiming all of it.
stories.outcome: Rav Pinchas bar Ami challenged them and they replied they had seized it in the river's current; the matter remains unresolved at the window's edge.
stories.summary: Yeimar bar Chashu was owed money by a man who died leaving a boat, and sent an agent to seize it. Rav Pappa and Rav Huna, who were also owed money, told the agent that seizing to others' detriment does not acquire, and took the boat themselves, one rowing and one pulling, each claiming all of it. Rav Pinchas bar Ami objected that such seizure works only in the public domain, and they answered they had taken it from the middle of the river.

stories.actor: Nakdimon ben Guryon's daughter-in-law
stories.event: The Sages awarded her two se'a of wine weekly for cooking from her late husband's estate.
stories.turn: She blessed them that their own daughters should receive the same.
stories.outcome: The Sages did not answer amen, since she was a widow awaiting levirate marriage.
stories.summary: The widowed daughter-in-law of Nakdimon ben Guryon was awarded a generous wine allowance by the Sages. She blessed them that their daughters should receive as much. Because she was a widow waiting for her yavam, they did not answer amen.

stories.actor: Choma, Abaye's widow, and Rava
stories.event: Choma came before Rava to claim sustenance and wine from Abaye's estate.
stories.turn: While showing the size of Abaye's cups her arm was uncovered and her beauty lit the court, stirring Rava.
stories.outcome: Rava's wife beat Choma with a chest lock and drove her out of Mechoza, accusing her of killing three husbands.
stories.summary: After Abaye died, his widow Choma asked Rava for sustenance and wine. Rava doubted Abaye drank wine; she insisted he gave her large cups, and as she gestured her arm was exposed and seemed to light up the court. Rava went home and asked his wife for relations; she learned Choma had been in court, chased her and beat her out of the city, saying she had already killed three husbands and was coming for another.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava
stories.event: She came before Rav Nechemya to claim sustenance and wine.
stories.turn: He granted wine because Mechoza residents drink wine.
stories.outcome: She received both sustenance and wine.
stories.summary: The widow of Rav Yosef son of Rava asked Rav Nechemya for sustenance, which he granted, and then for wine. He granted that too, explaining that the people of Mechoza are accustomed to drinking wine.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya of D'vil
stories.event: She came before Rav Yosef claiming sustenance, wine, and then silk garments.
stories.turn: Rav Yosef asked why she needed silk.
stories.outcome: She answered: for you, your friends and your friends' friends.
stories.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef and was granted sustenance and wine. When she asked for silk garments, he asked why. She replied that she needed them to appear properly before him and his colleagues.

stories.actor: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei
stories.event: Rabbi Elazar testified once in his life, about seeing a priest's slave receive teruma.
stories.turn: Because he testified in Rabbi Yehuda's region, where teruma is evidence of priesthood, the court sought to declare the slave a priest.
stories.outcome: The slave was nearly, but not actually, elevated to the priesthood on his testimony.
stories.summary: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yosei said he testified only once, and on his word a slave was almost made a priest. He had seen a priest's slave given teruma in Rabbi Yosei's region, where this proves nothing, and testified about it in Rabbi Yehuda's region, where receiving teruma establishes priestly lineage. The Gemara insists the court only sought to elevate the slave, since God would not let the righteous cause such an error.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi and Rabbi Chanina bar Chama
stories.event: In Rabbi's days people sought to declare Babylonian lineage inferior to that of Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: Rabbi, of Babylonian descent, protested and appointed Rabbi Chanina bar Chama to address them.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Chanina cited a tradition that Eretz Yisrael's lineage is muddled compared to Babylonia's.
stories.summary: During Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi's time, some wanted to treat Babylonian lineage as inferior. Rabbi, himself of Babylonian descent, asked if they were trying to insult him and sent Rabbi Chanina bar Chama to them. Rabbi Chanina told them his received tradition that Babylonia's lineage is the purest.

stories.actor: Rabbi Pinchas
stories.event: When people sought to declare Babylonian lineage inferior, Rabbi Pinchas arranged for servants to carry him off after he made two statements.
stories.turn: He announced a startling ruling on bird slaughter, then declared Eretz Yisrael's lineage inferior to Babylonia's, and was carried away.
stories.outcome: His pursuers could not catch him; they examined lineages until it became dangerous and stopped.
stories.summary: In Rabbi Pinchas's day there was a move to declare Babylonian lineage inferior. He told his servants to carry him off on a stretcher after his second statement in the study hall. He first said bird slaughter is not required by Torah law, and while they puzzled over it he declared Eretz Yisrael's lineage muddled compared to Babylonia's, and was carried off. They chased him in vain, then investigated families until they reached powerful ones and backed off.

stories.actor: Rava
stories.event: Rava served drinks at his son's wedding; some sages stood for him and others did not.
stories.turn: Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas did not stand.
stories.outcome: Rava became angry and asked whether they alone were sages.
stories.summary: At his son's wedding Rava poured drinks for the guests. Rav Pappa and Rav Huna stood when he approached, but Rav Mari and Rav Pinchas did not. Rava became angry, asking if they thought only they were sages.

stories.actor: Rav Pappa
stories.event: Rav Pappa served drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding.
stories.turn: Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda did not stand for him.
stories.outcome: Rav Pappa became angry.
stories.summary: Rav Pappa poured drinks at his son's wedding and gave a cup to Rabbi Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda, who did not stand for him. Rav Pappa was offended.

stories.actor: Rabban Gamliel, Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok
stories.event: At his son's wedding Rabban Gamliel, the Nasi, stood and served drinks to the sages.
stories.turn: Rabbi Eliezer refused the cup and rebuked Rabbi Yehoshua for accepting it.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yehoshua cited Abraham serving guests, and Rabbi Tzadok cited God serving all creatures, justifying Rabban Gamliel's service.
stories.summary: Rabban Gamliel served drinks to Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Tzadok at his son's wedding. Rabbi Eliezer refused and objected when Rabbi Yehoshua accepted. Rabbi Yehoshua answered that Abraham, greater still, served guests he thought were Arabs. Rabbi Tzadok added that God Himself provides for every creature, so Rabban Gamliel may serve them.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
stories.event: Rabbi Yishmael had two scholars judge a case for a litigant who had offered him a gift.
stories.turn: Walking back and forth, he caught himself thinking up arguments for that litigant.
stories.outcome: He cursed bribe-takers, reasoning that if he was biased without taking anything, they must be far worse.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yishmael seated two scholars to hear the case. While pacing, he kept thinking of claims the litigant could make. He exclaimed that if he, who took nothing that was not his own, was so affected, bribe-takers must be utterly biased.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha
stories.event: A man from far away brought Rabbi Yishmael, a priest, the first shearing.
stories.turn: Asked why he had passed other priests, the man revealed he had a case to bring before him.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yishmael refused the gift, disqualified himself, and found himself biased anyway while others judged.
stories.summary: A man brought Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha the first shearing from a distant town. When asked why, he admitted he had a case to present. Rabbi Yishmael refused the gift and declared himself disqualified; while others judged, he caught himself thinking up the man's arguments and cursed those who take bribes.

stories.actor: Rav Anan
stories.event: A man with a case brought Rav Anan a basket of small fish; Rav Anan refused it, then accepted it as a gift and sent him to Rav Nachman.
stories.turn: Rav Nachman assumed the man was Rav Anan's relative and gave him precedence, so the opposing litigant lost his nerve and the case.
stories.outcome: Elijah stopped visiting Rav Anan; after fasting and prayer Elijah returned but frightened him, and Rav Anan learned the rest of Seder Eliyahu from inside a box.
stories.summary: A litigant brought Rav Anan fish; Rav Anan disqualified himself, but accepted the gift when the man said he no longer wanted judgment. He sent the man to Rav Nachman with a note that he was disqualified, and Rav Nachman, thinking him a relative, put the orphans' case aside and honored him, so the other side was too intimidated to argue. Because of this, Elijah stopped visiting Rav Anan; Rav Anan fasted and prayed, Elijah returned in frightening forms, and Rav Anan sat in a box to finish learning from him.

stories.actor: Rav Yosef
stories.event: During a famine in Rav Yosef's years, the Sages asked him to pray for mercy.
stories.turn: He refused, comparing himself to Elisha, who supported 2,200 sages yet did not pray in time of divine anger.
stories.outcome: The window ends with his refusal.
stories.summary: In Rav Yosef's time there was a famine, and the Sages asked him to pray. He answered that Elisha, who fed thousands of sages, did not pray in such a time, so how could he.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi and the Angel of Death
stories.event: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was dying, the Angel of Death was told to do his bidding and showed him his place in paradise.
stories.turn: Having taken the angel's knife, he jumped into paradise and swore he would not come back.
stories.outcome: God let the oath stand, a Divine Voice made him return the knife, Elijah announced him, and he met Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai.
stories.summary: As Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi was about to die, the Angel of Death came to grant his wishes. He asked to see his place in paradise and to hold the angel's knife on the way, and on arrival he leapt over into paradise, swearing he would not leave. God ruled that since he had never had an oath annulled he could stay; a Divine Voice made him return the knife. In paradise Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai questioned him about rainbows, and he modestly said one had been seen in his time.

stories.actor: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa and the Angel of Death
stories.event: When Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa was dying, he got thirty days from the Angel of Death to review his learning, then asked for the knife.
stories.turn: The angel refused, suspecting the same trick as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, and said Rabbi Chanina had not studied among the ra'atan sufferers.
stories.outcome: He died, a pillar of fire separated him from everyone, and it departed only when Rabbi Alexandri appealed to his own honor.
stories.summary: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa, a friend of the Angel of Death, asked for thirty days to review his studies before dying, and got them. When he then asked for the angel's knife, the angel refused, asking if he meant to escape like his friend, and pointed out he had not studied among the ra'atan sufferers. At his death a pillar of fire surrounded him; Rabbi Alexandri asked it to leave for the Sages' honor and his father's, with no effect, and it left only when asked for his own honor.

stories.actor: A bead seller and a woman
stories.event: A woman asked a man selling glass beads for a string, and he asked if she would be betrothed by it.
stories.turn: She answered 'Give, give.'
stories.outcome: Rav Chama ruled that such an answer means nothing, so she is not betrothed.
stories.summary: A man was selling glass beads when a woman asked him for a string. He asked whether she would be betrothed to him if he gave it, and she said 'Give, give.' Rav Chama ruled that this mocking reply is meaningless.

stories.actor: A man drinking wine and a woman
stories.event: A woman asked a man drinking in a shop for a cup, and he asked if she would be betrothed by it.
stories.turn: She answered 'Give me to drink, give me to drink.'
stories.outcome: Rav Chama ruled the reply meaningless; she is not betrothed.
stories.summary: In a wine shop a woman asked a man for a cup of wine. He asked if she would be betrothed by it, and she replied 'Give me to drink.' Rav Chama ruled that she had not agreed.

stories.actor: A date picker and a woman
stories.event: A woman asked a man picking dates to throw her two, and he asked if she would be betrothed by them.
stories.turn: She answered 'Throw, throw.'
stories.outcome: Rav Zevid ruled the reply meaningless; she is not betrothed.
stories.summary: A man was picking dates when a woman asked him to throw her two. He asked if she would be betrothed by them, and she said 'Throw, throw.' Rav Zevid ruled that this means nothing.

stories.actor: A groom, his bride and Rabban Gamliel the Elder
stories.event: A groom complained to Rabban Gamliel that he found no blood on the wedding night.
stories.turn: The bride said she came from the Dorketi family who have no such blood, and Rabban Gamliel's investigation confirmed it.
stories.outcome: Rabban Gamliel told the groom to keep his acquisition and called him fortunate.
stories.summary: A man told Rabban Gamliel the Elder that his bride showed no virginal blood. She explained that her family, the Dorketi, never have menstrual or hymenal blood. Rabban Gamliel checked her relatives, found it true, and told the husband to keep his bride, calling him fortunate.

stories.actor: A groom, his bride and Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi
stories.event: During a famine, a groom complained to Rabbi that he found no blood, while his bride insisted she was a virgin.
stories.turn: Rabbi saw their faces were black with hunger and had them bathed, fed and given drink.
stories.outcome: The groom then found blood, and Rabbi told him to keep his acquisition.
stories.summary: In years of drought, a man complained to Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi that he found no blood with his bride, who said she was still a virgin. Seeing they were starved, Rabbi had them bathed and fed and sent them to a room. This time the groom found blood, and Rabbi quoted a verse about skin shriveled on bones.

stories.actor: Shmuel
stories.event: A man gave Shmuel a hand as he got off a ferry.
stories.turn: The man turned out to have a case to bring before him.
stories.outcome: Shmuel disqualified himself from judging it.
stories.summary: As Shmuel was crossing on a ferry, a man helped him with his hand. When Shmuel learned the man had a case for him, he declared himself disqualified because of the favor.

stories.actor: Ameimar
stories.event: While Ameimar sat in judgment, a man removed a feather from his head.
stories.turn: The man had a case to bring before him.
stories.outcome: Ameimar disqualified himself.
stories.summary: A feather landed on Ameimar's head as he judged, and a man brushed it off. Learning the man had a case, Ameimar said he could not judge it.

stories.actor: Mar Ukva
stories.event: A man covered spittle lying in front of Mar Ukva.
stories.turn: The man had a case to bring before him.
stories.outcome: Mar Ukva disqualified himself.
stories.summary: A man covered some spittle in front of Mar Ukva. When he said he had a case, Mar Ukva declared himself disqualified.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei and his sharecropper
stories.event: His sharecropper brought the weekly fruit basket on Thursday instead of Friday.
stories.turn: Asked why, the sharecropper said he had a case to bring that day.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yishmael refused the fruit, had two scholars judge the case, caught himself biased anyway, and cursed bribe-takers.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yishmael's sharecropper usually brought him fruit every Friday but came on Thursday. He explained that he had a case to bring before him. Rabbi Yishmael refused the basket and appointed two scholars to judge; pacing about, he found himself thinking up arguments for the sharecropper and cursed those who take bribes.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha
stories.event: A man from far away brought Rabbi Yishmael the first shearing.
stories.turn: Asked why he came so far, the man revealed he had a case to bring.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yishmael disqualified himself and refused the gift.
stories.summary: A man brought Rabbi Yishmael bar Elisha the first shearing from a distant place. When asked why, he admitted he had a case. Rabbi Yishmael refused the gift and declared himself disqualified.

stories.actor: A man and a woman washing her feet
stories.event: A man grabbed coins from another person, threw them to a woman, and declared her betrothed.
stories.turn: He came to Rava to ask about her status.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the betrothal void, since the coins were stolen.
stories.summary: A woman was washing her feet when a man snatched some coins from someone else and threw them to her, saying she was betrothed to him. Rava ruled that no one follows Rabbi Shimon's view that a robbery victim despairs, so the stolen money did not betroth her.

stories.actor: A sharecropper
stories.event: A sharecropper betrothed a woman with a handful of onions from the field he worked.
stories.turn: He asked Rava about it.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the onions were not his, since the owner had not permitted it.
stories.summary: A sharecropper used a handful of onions from his landlord's field to betroth a woman. Rava asked him who had given him permission, implying the onions were stolen and the betrothal invalid.

stories.actor: A brewer
stories.event: A brewer betrothed a woman with sediment from someone else's beer, and the owner told him to use the better sediment instead.
stories.turn: The brewer asked Rava whether the owner's remark meant consent.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled the owner spoke from embarrassment, so she is not betrothed.
stories.summary: A brewer betrothed a woman with sediment from beer he was making for someone else. The owner found him and asked why he did not use the better sediment. Rava ruled that such a remark counts as consent only for teruma; here the owner spoke from embarrassment, and the woman is not betrothed.

stories.actor: A man who betrothed with a myrtle branch
stories.event: A man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace.
stories.turn: Rav Acha bar Huna sent the case to Rav Yosef.
stories.outcome: Rav Yosef ordered him flogged and required a bill of divorce.
stories.summary: A man betrothed a woman in the market with a myrtle branch. Rav Acha bar Huna asked Rav Yosef what to do. Rav Yosef answered to flog him, as Rav would, and require a divorce, as Shmuel would.

stories.actor: A son-in-law and Rav Sheshet
stories.event: A son-in-law passed by the door of his father-in-law's house.
stories.turn: There were rumors about him and his mother-in-law.
stories.outcome: Rav Sheshet had him flogged.
stories.summary: A son-in-law walked past his father-in-law's house, and Rav Sheshet had him flogged. The Gemara explains that he was suspected of an affair with his mother-in-law.

stories.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
stories.event: The two sages seized a dead debtor's boat, each claiming all of it.
stories.turn: Rav Pinchas bar Ami challenged them, and Rava called them white geese who take people's cloaks.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled that seizure counts only if made while the debtor was alive, so they had no claim.
stories.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna seized a dead man's boat, one steering and one pulling, each claiming it all. Rav Pinchas bar Ami questioned whether they could acquire it, and they said they took it from the river's current. When they went to Rava, he scolded them as white-bearded geese stealing cloaks and ruled that a seizure is valid only during the debtor's lifetime.

stories.actor: Chama son of Rabba bar Abbahu
stories.event: Chama, sent by Avimi to repay a debt in Bei Chozai, paid and asked for the loan document.
stories.turn: The creditors said the payment was for a different, unwritten debt.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Abbahu ruled that without witnesses to the payment, the creditors are believed.
stories.summary: Avimi son of Rabbi Abbahu sent Chama to repay his creditors in Bei Chozai. Chama paid and asked for the document, but they claimed the money went toward another debt. Rabbi Abbahu asked if he had witnesses; he had none, so the creditors, who could have denied being paid at all, were believed.

stories.actor: A woman holding a bag of documents
stories.event: The heirs demanded a bag of documents deposited with a woman, who claimed she seized it during the depositor's life.
stories.turn: Rav Nachman asked if she had witnesses that he demanded it and she refused, and she had none.
stories.outcome: Rav Nachman ruled it a seizure after death, which is worthless.
stories.summary: A woman held a bag of documents on deposit, and the heirs came to claim it. She said she had seized it for a debt while the owner was alive. Rav Nachman asked for witnesses, and when she had none he ruled that it was a seizure after death and void.

stories.actor: A depositor and Rabbi Meyasha's heirs
stories.event: A man deposited seven pearls with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without instructions.
stories.turn: The dispute came before Rabbi Ami.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Ami awarded the pearls to the depositor, since Rabbi Meyasha was not wealthy and the man gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man left seven pearls wrapped in a sheet with Rabbi Meyasha, who died without saying whose they were. Rabbi Ami ruled for the depositor, because he knew Rabbi Meyasha was not rich and the man could identify the pearls.

stories.actor: A depositor and Chasa's heirs
stories.event: A man deposited a silver goblet with Chasa, who died without instructions.
stories.turn: The dispute came before Rav Nachman.
stories.outcome: Rav Nachman awarded it to the depositor, since Chasa was not wealthy and the man gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man left a silver goblet with Chasa, who died without leaving word. Rav Nachman ruled it belonged to the depositor, since Chasa was not wealthy and the man identified it.

stories.actor: A depositor and Rav Dimi's heirs
stories.event: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without instructions.
stories.turn: The dispute came before Rabbi Abba.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Abba awarded it to the depositor, since Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the man gave an identifying mark.
stories.summary: A man left silk with Rav Dimi, brother of Rav Safra, who died without instructions. Rabbi Abba ruled for the depositor, since Rav Dimi was not rich and the man could identify the silk.

stories.actor: Choma, Abaye's widow, and Rava
stories.event: Choma came before Rava to claim sustenance and wine from Abaye's estate.
stories.turn: While showing the size of Abaye's cups her arm was uncovered and her beauty lit the court, stirring Rava.
stories.outcome: Rava's wife beat Choma with a chest lock and drove her out of Mechoza, accusing her of killing three husbands.
stories.summary: After Abaye died, Choma asked Rava for sustenance and wine. Rava doubted Abaye drank wine; as she showed him the size of Abaye's cups, her arm was exposed and seemed to light up the court. Rava went home and asked his wife for relations; she found out Choma had been in court, chased her and beat her out of Mechoza, saying she had killed three husbands and now wanted another.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rava
stories.event: She came before Rav Nechemya to claim sustenance and wine.
stories.turn: He granted wine because Mechoza residents drink wine.
stories.outcome: She received both sustenance and wine.
stories.summary: The widow of Rav Yosef son of Rava asked Rav Nechemya for sustenance and then wine. He granted both, explaining that people in Mechoza drink wine.

stories.actor: The wife of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya of D'vil
stories.event: She came before Rav Yosef claiming sustenance, wine, and then silk garments.
stories.turn: Rav Yosef asked why she needed silk.
stories.outcome: She answered: for you, your friends and your friends' friends.
stories.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef and was granted sustenance and wine. When she asked for silk, he asked why, and she said it was so she could appear properly before him and his colleagues.

stories.actor: A belt seller and a man
stories.event: A man snatched a belt from a woman selling belts and asked if she would be betrothed if he gave it back.
stories.turn: She took it and said nothing.
stories.outcome: Rav Nachman ruled she could say she merely took back her own property, so she is not betrothed.
stories.summary: A man grabbed a belt from a woman who sold them. When she asked for it back, he asked if she would be betrothed to him by it; she took it in silence. Rav Nachman ruled that she was only taking what was hers.

stories.actor: A man who sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael
stories.event: A man sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: He went but could not settle there.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled he could cancel the sale, or in another version that he could not.
stories.summary: A man sold his property so he could move to Eretz Yisrael. He went, but could not settle there, and came back wanting the sale undone. Rava ruled that the intention was to settle, so the sale is void; another version reports the opposite ruling.

stories.actor: A man who sold his property but did not go
stories.event: A man sold his property intending to move to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: In the end he did not go.
stories.outcome: Rav Ashi ruled the sale stands, since he could have gone had he wanted.
stories.summary: Another man sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael but never went. Rav Ashi ruled that he could have gone if he wished, so the sale is not cancelled.
